body.x: Keiser Inc. (CEO DuHeon Gyeon) announced that it recorded USD 10.16 million (approximately 14.817 billion KRW) in export consultation value for its copyright-specialized content technology and services at CES 2026, the world’s largest IT and tech exhibition held in Las Vegas early last month.

Keiser operates JIGPU, an integrated content platform that supports searching for and recommending specific sound sources, as well as usage, settlement, and transaction processing, powered by its self-developed Genre Component Combination (GCC) search engine.

In today’s digitized content production environment, the boundary between creators and users blurs, and unexpected copyright infringements frequently occur among video producers when using sound sources. Accordingly, Keiser earns a strong reputation in the industry by offering a platform that combines AI (Artificial Intelligence) and blockchain technology with an integrated copyright system.

In fact, Keiser attracted TIPS investment (KVIC) with JIGPU, which officially launched and began service last year, and stood out by partnering with 500 music producers to release over 1,000 songs on its platform from the outset. Furthermore, the company firmly established a foundation for global expansion while developing a system for contracting local artists and releasing audio content overseas.

body.cap: Introductory image of Keiser’s Genre Component Combination (GCC) search engine | Image provided by Keiser

body.x: In particular, the GCC search engine, the foundation of the JIGPU platform, won the Innovation Award in the Content and Entertainment category at CES 2026, gaining recognition for its technological practicality and marketability, and as a result, it attracted the attention of many global visitors, influential buyers, and partners at the exhibition site.

Thanks to the active enthusiasm of attendees, Keiser attracted 65 consultations during this year’s CES period and recorded a total of 10.16 million USD in consultations. Through this, the company also signed MOUs (Memorandum of Understanding) for business cooperation and technology development with HI-FIVE Co., Ltd (CEO Chan Wook Kim), which supports sound source publishing and copyright management for domestic and foreign artists and writers, and Mand.ro (CEO Sangho Yi), a robot hand specialist company.

A Keiser official stated, “We feel very pleased that leading companies in each industry recognized the technological value of Keiser’s solutions presented at this CES.” They added, “As we confirmed the potential as an actual business model beyond simple technological display, we plan to cooperate closely with new partners to accelerate technological advancement and settlement in the global market.”

They continued, “The scale of consultation value recorded during the four-day exhibition shows that our company can exert sufficient competitiveness in the global market.” They expressed their ambition, saying, “We will use this achievement as a stepping stone to leap forward as a next-generation global unicorn company.”

Incheon Metropolitan City and the Incheon Free Economic Zone Authority announced that they will establish the INCHEON-IFEZ Pavilion in the LVCC North Hall at CES 2026, showcasing Incheon’s urban vision and innovative technologies as the city evolves from smart city development into the AI era. By linking various exhibition programs—including the 10 companies participating in the INCHEON-IFEZ Pavilion, Eureka Park, global pavilions, and the CES Innovation Award Showcase—the organizations will support the participation of 51 Incheon-based innovative companies at CES. Notably, 14 companies received CES Innovation Awards across 17 categories, marking a record-high achievement and demonstrating the technological competitiveness and global growth potential of Incheon’s innovation companies.
